brief: Slovakia's analytical-intermediary layer for banking and payments splits cleanly by language and channel: English-language commercial research houses (GlobalData, Argus Advisory, Verisk Financial, Statista) sell country cards-and-payments sizing and forecasts with only abstracts free, while rating agencies (Moody's with free rating-action press releases; Fitch/S&P apparently gated) and the IMF FSAP supply the most rigorous free sector metrics. In Slovak, the productive channels are institutional rather than commercial — the IFP think tank at the Ministry of Finance via analyzy.gov.sk, the SBA's štatistiky a analýzy section with its Ipsos-run perception surveys, the tripartite sector council's SWOT analysis of banking and payment services, and NBS research papers on cash in circulation and digital-euro attitudes. A noisy but high-frequency stratum consists of scheme-commissioned surveys (Mastercard/Visa) distributed through SK press wires and finance portals (oPeniazoch, Finsider, FinReport); these carry usable cash-vs-card-vs-mobile splits but are promotional and must always be traced back to fieldwork details. The biggest remaining gaps are bank-owned economic research units and SK academic repositories, neither of which was covered in this pass.
